335: # Hardened release profile for shipping to end users (alpha + stable).
336: # Use `cargo build --profile release-dist` for distribution builds.
337: # Not used by default `--release` to avoid slowing down local dev builds (~2.2x).
338: #
339: # Hardening: thin LTO for cross-crate optimization with reasonable link times,
340: # codegen-units=1 maximizes optimization (whole-program analysis, no CGU boundaries).
341: # debug=1 emits line-tables DWARF; strip=false keeps symbols so CI can extract
342: # .debug sidecars (Linux) or .dSYM bundles (macOS) before stripping post-build.
343: # Linker flags (RELRO, NX stack) are set per-target in .cargo/config.toml.
344: [profile.release-dist]
345: inherits = "release"
346: lto = "thin"
347: codegen-units = 1
348: strip = false
349: debug = 1
350: split-debuginfo = "off"
351: 
352: # Production profile for latency-sensitive x-product services (VF, home-mixer).
353: # Thin LTO gives ~90% of full LTO benefit at significantly faster link time.
354: # Keeps symbols + line tables for prod debuggability (perf, flamegraph, stack traces).
355: [profile.x-prod]
356: inherits = "release"
357: lto = "thin"
358: strip = false
359: codegen-units = 1
360: debug = "line-tables-only"
361: panic = "unwind"

363: # Desktop release profile. Functionally identical to release-dist — kept as a
364: # named alias so the desktop workflow can reference it without coupling to the
365: # CLI pipeline's profile name. Alpha and stable share a single release-dist
366: # profile so that stable promotion can pointer-swap the alpha binary without
367: # rebuilding.

1: # AGENTS.md
2: 
3: This file provides guidance to AI coding agents working on the `skills` CLI codebase.
4: 
5: ## Project Overview
6: 
7: `skills` is the CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem.
8: 
9: ## Commands
10: 
11: | Command                       | Description                                         |
12: | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
13: | `skills`                      | Show banner with available commands                 |
14: | `skills add <pkg>`            | Install skills from git repos, URLs, or local paths |
15: | `skills use <pkg>@<skill>`    | Use one skill without installing                    |
16: | `skills experimental_install` | Restore skills from skills-lock.json                |
17: | `skills experimental_sync`    | Sync skills from node_modules into agent dirs       |
18: | `skills list`                 | List installed skills (alias: `ls`)                 |
19: | `skills update [skills...]`   | Update skills to latest versions                    |
20: | `skills init [name]`          | Create a new SKILL.md template                      |
21: 
22: Aliases: `skills a` works for `add`. `skills i`, `skills install` (no args) restore from `skills-lock.json`. `skills ls` works for `list`. `skills experimental_install` restores from `skills-lock.json`. `skills experimental_sync` crawls `node_modules` for skills.
23: 
24: ## Architecture
25: 
26: ```
27: src/
28: ├── cli.ts           # Main entry point, command routing, init/check/update
29: ├── cli.test.ts      # CLI tests
30: ├── add.ts           # Core add command logic
31: ├── add-prompt.test.ts # Add prompt behavior tests
32: ├── add.test.ts      # Add command tests
33: ├── constants.ts      # Shared constants
34: ├── find.ts           # Find/search command
35: ├── list.ts          # List installed skills command
36: ├── list.test.ts     # List command tests
37: ├── remove.ts         # Remove command implementation
38: ├── remove.test.ts    # Remove command tests
39: ├── agents.ts        # Agent definitions and detection
40: ├── installer.ts     # Skill installation logic (symlink/copy) + listInstalledSkills
41: ├── skills.ts        # Skill discovery and parsing
42: ├── skill-lock.ts    # Global lock file management (~/.agents/.skill-lock.json)
43: ├── local-lock.ts    # Local lock file management (skills-lock.json, checked in)
44: ├── sync.ts          # Sync command - crawl node_modules for skills
45: ├── source-parser.ts # Parse git URLs, GitHub shorthand, local paths
46: ├── git.ts           # Git clone operations
47: ├── telemetry.ts     # Anonymous usage tracking
48: ├── types.ts         # TypeScript types
49: ├── mintlify.ts      # Mintlify skill fetching (legacy)
50: ├── plugin-manifest.ts # Plugin manifest discovery support
51: ├── prompts/         # Interactive prompt helpers
52: │   └── search-multiselect.ts
53: ├── providers/       # Remote skill providers (GitHub, HuggingFace, Mintlify)
54: │   ├── index.ts
55: │   ├── registry.ts
56: │   ├── types.ts
57: │   ├── huggingface.ts
58: │   ├── mintlify.ts
59: │   └── wellknown.ts
60: ├── init.test.ts     # Init command tests
61: ├── use.ts           # Use command - generate a skill prompt or launch an agent
62: ├── use.test.ts      # Use command tests
63: └── test-utils.ts    # Test utilities
64: 
65: tests/
66: ├── cross-platform-paths.test.ts # Path normalization across platforms
67: ├── full-depth-discovery.test.ts # --full-depth skill discovery tests
68: ├── openclaw-paths.test.ts       # OpenClaw-specific path tests
69: ├── plugin-manifest-discovery.test.ts # Plugin manifest skill discovery
70: ├── sanitize-name.test.ts     # Tests for sanitizeName (path traversal prevention)
71: ├── skill-matching.test.ts    # Tests for filterSkills (multi-word skill name matching)
72: ├── source-parser.test.ts     # Tests for URL/path parsing
73: ├── installer-symlink.test.ts # Tests for symlink installation
74: ├── list-installed.test.ts    # Tests for listing installed skills
75: ├── skill-path.test.ts        # Tests for skill path handling
76: ├── wellknown-provider.test.ts # Tests for well-known provider
77: ├── xdg-config-paths.test.ts   # XDG global path handling tests
78: └── dist.test.ts               # Tests for built distribution
79: ```
80: 
81: ## Update Checking System
82: 
83: ### How `skills check` and `skills update` Work
84: 
85: 1. Read `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` for installed skills
86: 2. Filter to GitHub-backed skills that have both `skillFolderHash` and `skillPath`
87: 3. For each skill, call `fetchSkillFolderHash(source, skillPath, token)`. Optional auth token is sourced from `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, or `gh auth token` to improve rate limits.
88: 4. `fetchSkillFolderHash` calls GitHub Trees API directly (`/git/trees/<branch>?recursive=1` for `main`, then `master` fallback)
89: 5. Compare latest folder tree SHA with lock file `skillFolderHash`; mismatch means update available
90: 6. `skills update` reinstalls changed skills by invoking the current CLI entrypoint directly (`node <repo>/bin/cli.mjs add <source-tree-url> -g -y`) to avoid nested npm exec/npx behavior
91: 
92: ### Lock File Compatibility
93: 
94: The lock file format is v3. Key field: `skillFolderHash` (GitHub tree SHA for the skill folder).
95: 
96: If reading an older lock file version, it's wiped. Users must reinstall skills to populate the new format.
97: 
98: ## Key Integration Points
99: 
100: | Feature                    | Implementation                                                |
101: | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
102: | `skills add`               | `src/add.ts` - full implementation                            |
103: | `skills experimental_sync` | `src/sync.ts` - crawl node_modules                            |
104: | `skills check`             | `src/cli.ts` + `fetchSkillFolderHash` in `src/skill-lock.ts`  |
105: | `skills update`            | `src/cli.ts` direct hash compare + reinstall via `skills add` |
106: 
107: ## Development
108: 
109: ```bash
110: # Install dependencies
111: pnpm install
112: 
113: # Build
114: pnpm build
115:

313:   const restArgs = args.slice(1);

315:   // Subcommand --help / -h must short-circuit before dispatch so that running
316:   // e.g. `skills update --help` prints help instead of executing the update
317:   // flow. Without this pre-check, every subcommand handler that doesn't
318:   // inspect `--help` itself ends up running its side-effecting work.
319:   if (
320:     command !== '--help' &&
321:     command !== '-h' &&
322:     command !== '--version' &&
323:     command !== '-v' &&
324:     (restArgs.includes('--help') || restArgs.includes('-h'))
325:   ) {
326:     if (command === 'remove' || command === 'rm' || command === 'r') {
327:       showRemoveHelp();
328:     } else {
329:       showHelp();
330:     }
331:     return;
332:   }
333: 
334:   switch (command) {
335:     case 'find':
336:     case 'search':
337:     case 'f':
338:     case 's':
339:       if (!inAgent) showLogo();
340:       console.log();
341:       await runFind(restArgs);
342:       break;
343:     case 'init':
344:       if (!inAgent) showLogo();
345:       console.log();
346:       runInit(restArgs);
347:       break;
348:     case 'experimental_install': {
349:       if (!inAgent) showLogo();
350:       await runInstallFromLock(restArgs);

352:     }
353:     case 'i':
354:     case 'install':
355:     case 'a':
356:     case 'add': {
357:       if (!inAgent) showLogo();
358:       const { source: addSource, options: addOpts, errors } = parseAddOptions(restArgs);
359:       if (errors.length > 0) {
360:         for (const error of errors) console.error(`Error: ${error}`);
361:         process.exitCode = 1;

392:       break;

395:     case 'upgrade':

233:         await rm(linkPath, { recursive: true });
234:       }
235:     } catch (err: unknown) {
236:       // ELOOP = circular symlink, ENOENT = doesn't exist
237:       // For ELOOP, try to remove the broken symlink
238:       if (err && typeof err === 'object' && 'code' in err && err.code === 'ELOOP') {
239:         try {
240:           await rm(linkPath, { force: true });
241:         } catch {
242:           // If we can't remove it, symlink creation will fail and trigger copy fallback
243:         }
244:       }
245:       // For ENOENT or other errors, continue to symlink creation
246:     }
247: 
248:     const linkDir = dirname(linkPath);
249:     await mkdir(linkDir, { recursive: true });
250: 
251:     // Use the real (symlink-resolved) parent directory for computing the relative path.
252:     // This ensures the symlink target is correct even when the link's parent dir is a symlink.
253:     const realLinkDir = await resolveParentSymlinks(linkDir);
254:     const relativePath = relative(realLinkDir, target);
255:     const symlinkType = platform() === 'win32' ? 'junction' : undefined;
256:     const symlinkTarget = symlinkType === 'junction' ? resolvedTarget : relativePath;
257: 
258:     await symlink(symlinkTarget, linkPath, symlinkType);
259:     return true;
260:   } catch {
261:     return false;
262:   }
263: }

265: export async function installSkillForAgent(
266:   skill: Skill,
267:   agentType: AgentType,
268:   options: { global?: boolean; cwd?: string; mode?: InstallMode; eveSubagent?: string } = {}
269: ): Promise<InstallResult> {
270:   const agent = agents[agentType];
271:   const isGlobal = options.global ?? false;
272:   const cwd = options.cwd || process.cwd();
273:   const eveSubagent = options.eveSubagent;
274: 
275:   // Check if agent supports global installation
276:   if (isGlobal && agent.globalSkillsDir === undefined) {
277:     return {
278:       success: false,
279:       path: '',
280:       mode: options.mode ?? 'symlink',
281:       error: `${agent.displayName} does not support global skill installation`,
282:     };
283:   }
284: 
285:   // Sanitize skill name to prevent directory traversal
286:   const rawSkillName = skill.name || basename(skill.path);
287:   const skillName = sanitizeName(rawSkillName);
288: 
289:   const installMode = options.mode ?? 'symlink';
290: 
291:   // Canonical location: .agents/skills/<skill-name>
292:   const canonicalBase =
293:     agentType === 'eve' && installMode === 'symlink'
294:       ? getAgentBaseDir(agentType, isGlobal, cwd, eveSubagent)
295:       : getCanonicalSkillsDir(isGlobal, cwd);
296:   const canonicalDir = join(canonicalBase, skillName);
297: 
298:   // Agent-specific location (for symlink)
299:   const agentBase = getAgentBaseDir(agentType, isGlobal, cwd, eveSubagent);
300:   const agentDir = join(agentBase, skillName);
301: 
302:   // Validate paths
303:   if (!isPathSafe(canonicalBase, canonicalDir)) {
304:     return {
305:       success: false,
306:       path: agentDir,
307:       mode: installMode,
308:       error: 'Invalid skill name: potential path traversal detected',
309:     };
310:   }
311: 
312:   if (!isPathSafe(agentBase, agentDir)) {
313:     return {
314:       success: false,
315:       path: agentDir,
316:       mode: installMode,
317:       error: 'Invalid skill name: potential path traversal detected',
318:     };
319:   }
320: 
321:   try {
322:     // Never install onto (or inside) the source directory. This can happen with
323:     // agent-specific project directories like OpenClaw's "skills" when users run
324:     // `skills add ./skills --all`: the source `./skills/<name>` and destination
325:     // `./skills/<name>` are the same path. Cleaning the destination would delete
326:     // the user's source skill before we can link or copy it.
327:     if (pathsOverlap(skill.path, agentDir)) {
328:       return {
329:         success: true,
330:         path: agentDir,
331:         mode: installMode,
332:         skipped: true,
333:       };
334:     }
335: 
336:     // For copy mode, skip canonical directory and copy directly to agent location
337:     if (installMode === 'copy') {
338:       await cleanAndCreateDirectory(agentDir);
339:       await copyDirectory(skill.path, agentDir, agentType);
340: 
341:       return {
342:         success: true,
343:         path: agentDir,
344:         mode: 'copy',
345:       };
346:     }
347: 
348:     if (pathsOverlap(skill.path, canonicalDir)) {
349:       return {
350:         success: true,
351:         path: canonicalDir,
352:         canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
353:         mode: 'symlink',
354:         skipped: true,
355:       };
356:     }
357: 
358:     // Symlink mode: copy to canonical location and symlink to agent location
359:     await cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir);
360:     await copyDirectory(skill.path, canonicalDir, agentType);
361: 
362:     // For universal agents with global install, the skill is already in the canonical
363:     // ~/.agents/skills directory. Skip creating a symlink to the agent-specific global dir
364:     // (e.g. ~/.copilot/skills) to avoid duplicates.
365:     if (isGlobal && isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
366:       return {
367:         success: true,
368:         path: canonicalDir,
369:         canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
370:         mode: 'symlink',
371:       };
372:     }
373: 
374:     // For project-level installs, skip creating symlinks for non-universal agents
375:     // whose config directory doesn't already exist in the project. This prevents
376:     // creating directories like .windsurf/, .kiro/, etc. when those agents aren't
377:     // actually used in this project. The skill is already available in .agents/skills/.
378:     if (!isGlobal && !isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
379:       const agentRootDir = join(cwd, agents[agentType].skillsDir.split('/')[0]!);
380:       if (!existsSync(agentRootDir) && agentType !== 'claude-code') {
381:         return {
382:           success: true,
383:           path: canonicalDir,
384:           canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
385:           mode: 'symlink',
386:           skipped: true,
387:         };
388:       }
389:     }
390: 
391:     const symlinkCreated = await createSymlink(canonicalDir, agentDir);
392: 
393:     if (!symlinkCreated) {
394:       // Symlink failed, fall back to copy
395:       await cleanAndCreateDirectory(agentDir);
396:       await copyDirectory(skill.path, agentDir, agentType);
397: 
398:       return {
399:         success: true,
400:         path: agentDir,
401:         canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
402:         mode: 'symlink',
403:         symlinkFailed: true,
404:       };
405:     }
406: 
407:     return {
408:       success: true,
409:       path: agentDir,
410:       canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
411:       mode: 'symlink',
412:     };
413:   } catch (error) {
414:     return {
415:       success: false,
416:       path: agentDir,
417:       mode: installMode,
418:       error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error',
419:     };
420:   }
421: }

432: function stripIgnoredEveFrontmatter(raw: string): string {
433:   const { data, content } = parseFrontmatter(raw);
434:   const eveData: Record<string, unknown> = {};
435: 
436:   if (typeof data.description === 'string') {
437:     eveData.description = data.description;
438:   }
439:   if (typeof data.license === 'string') {
440:     eveData.license = data.license;
441:   }
442:   if (data.metadata && typeof data.metadata === 'object' && !Array.isArray(data.metadata)) {
443:     const metadata = Object.fromEntries(
444:       Object.entries(data.metadata).filter(
445:         (entry): entry is [string, string] => typeof entry[1] === 'string'
446:       )
447:     );
448:     if (Object.keys(metadata).length > 0) {
449:       eveData.metadata = metadata;
450:     }
451:   }
452: 
453:   const keys = Object.keys(eveData);
454:   if (keys.length === 0) {
455:     return content.replace(/^\r?\n/u, '');
456:   }
457: 
458:   const frontmatter = keys.map((key) => `${key}: ${JSON.stringify(eveData[key])}`).join('\n');
459:   return `---\n${frontmatter}\n---\n${content.replace(/^\r?\n/u, '')}`;
460: }

462: async function copyDirectory(src: string, dest: string, agentType?: AgentType): Promise<void> {
463:   await mkdir(dest, { recursive: true });
464: 
465:   const entries = await readdir(src, { withFileTypes: true });
466: 
467:   // Copy files and directories in parallel
468:   await Promise.all(
469:     entries
470:       .filter((entry) => !isExcluded(entry.name, entry.isDirectory()))
471:       .map(async (entry) => {
472:         const srcPath = join(src, entry.name);
473:         const destPath = join(dest, entry.name);
474: 
475:         if (entry.isDirectory()) {
476:           await copyDirectory(srcPath, destPath, agentType);
477:         } else {
478:           try {
479:             if (agentType === 'eve' && entry.name.toLowerCase() === 'skill.md') {
480:               await writeFile(
481:                 destPath,
482:                 stripIgnoredEveFrontmatter(await readFile(srcPath, 'utf-8'))
483:               );
484:               return;
485:             }
486: 
487:             await cp(srcPath, destPath, {
488:               // If the file is a symlink to elsewhere in a remote skill, it may not
489:               // resolve correctly once it has been copied to the local location.
490:               // `dereference: true` tells Node to copy the file instead of copying
491:               // the symlink. `recursive: true` handles symlinks pointing to directories.
492:               dereference: true,
493:               recursive: true,
494:             });
495:             const sourceStats = await stat(srcPath);
496:             await chmod(destPath, sourceStats.mode & 0o777);
497:           } catch (err: unknown) {
498:             // Skip broken symlinks (e.g., pointing to absolute paths on another machine)
499:             // instead of aborting the entire install.
500:             if (
501:               err instanceof Error &&
502:               'code' in err &&
503:               (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT' &&
504:               entry.isSymbolicLink()
505:             ) {
506:               console.warn(`Skipping broken symlink: ${srcPath}`);
507:             } else {
508:               throw err;
509:             }
510:           }
511:         }
512:       })
513:   );
514: }

811:   /**
812:    * Write all skill files to a directory (assumes directory already exists)

814:   async function writeSkillFiles(targetDir: string): Promise<void> {
815:     for (const [filePath, content] of skill.files) {
816:       // Validate file path doesn't escape the target directory
817:       const fullPath = join(targetDir, filePath);
818:       if (!isPathSafe(targetDir, fullPath)) {
819:         continue; // Skip files that would escape the directory
820:       }
821:

824:       if (parentDir !== targetDir) {
825:         await mkdir(parentDir, { recursive: true });

829:         fullPath,

831:           basename(filePath).toLowerCase() === 'skill.md' &&

848:         mode: 'copy',

850:     }

853:     await cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir);
854:     await writeSkillFiles(canonicalDir);

856:     // For universal agents with global install, skip creating agent-specific symlink
857:     if (isGlobal && isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
858:       return {
859:         success: true,
860:         path: canonicalDir,
861:         canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
862:         mode: 'symlink',
863:       };
864:     }
865: 
866:     const symlinkCreated = await createSymlink(canonicalDir, agentDir);
867: 
868:     if (!symlinkCreated) {
869:       // Symlink failed, fall back to copy
870:       await cleanAndCreateDirectory(agentDir);
871:       await writeSkillFiles(agentDir);
872: 
873:       return {
874:         success: true,
875:         path: agentDir,
876:         canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
877:         mode: 'symlink',
878:         symlinkFailed: true,
879:       };
880:     }
881: 
882:     return {
883:       success: true,
884:       path: agentDir,
885:       canonicalPath: canonicalDir,
886:       mode: 'symlink',
887:     };
888:   } catch (error) {
889:     return {
890:       success: false,

1: //! # xai-grok-hooks
2: //!
3: //! Runtime hook system for Grok — file-based discovery, command execution,
4: //! and policy enforcement.
5: //!
6: //! ## Overview
7: //!
8: //! This crate provides a minimal hooks system for Grok. Hooks are discovered
9: //! from dedicated directories (`~/.grok/hooks/` and `<git-worktree-root>/.grok/hooks/`),
10: //! defined in JSON files (compatible settings format), and executed as child processes.
11: //!
12: //! ## v0 scope
13: //!
14: //! - Four event types: `session_start`, `pre_tool_use`, `post_tool_use`, `session_end`
15: //! - Command-backed hooks only
16: //! - `pre_tool_use` hooks can deny/allow (blocking); all others are non-blocking
17: //! - Fail-open by default: hook failures do not block normal operation
18: //!
19: //! ## Quick start
20: //!
21: //! ```rust,no_run
22: //! use std::path::Path;
23: //! use xai_grok_hooks::discovery::load_hooks;
24: //! use xai_grok_hooks::event::HookEventName;
25: //!
26: //! let (registry, errors) = load_hooks(
27: //!     Some(Path::new("/home/user/.grok/hooks")),
28: //!     Some(Path::new("/project/.grok/hooks")),
29: //! );
30: //!
31: //! for err in &errors {
32: //!     eprintln!("hook load warning: {err}");
33: //! }
34: //!
35: //! let pre_hooks = registry.hooks_for(HookEventName::PreToolUse);
36: //! println!("loaded {} pre_tool_use hooks", pre_hooks.len());
37: //! ```

13: pub struct WorkflowRunParams {
14:     pub script: String,
15:     pub args: serde_json::Value,
16:     pub journal: Journal,
17:     pub host_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<WorkflowHostRequest>,
18:     pub cancel: CancellationToken,
19:     pub max_ops: u64,
20: }
21: 
22: impl WorkflowRunParams {
23:     pub const DEFAULT_MAX_OPS: u64 = 100_000_000;
24: }
25: 
26: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
27: enum ControlToken {
28:     Complete(serde_json::Value),
29:     Pause(PauseKind, String),
30:     Budget(String),
31:     Cancelled,
32:     Fatal(String),
33: }
34: 
35: struct Ctx {
36:     host_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<WorkflowHostRequest>,
37:     journal: Journal,
38:     seq: u64,
39: }
40: 
41: impl Ctx {
42:     fn replaying(&self) -> bool {
43:         self.journal.covers(self.seq)
44:     }
45: 
46:     fn next_seq(&mut self) -> ScriptResult<u64> {
47:         Ok(self.reserve_seqs(1)?.start)
48:     }
49: 
50:     fn reserve_seqs(&mut self, count: usize) -> ScriptResult<std::ops::Range<u64>> {
51:         let count = u64::try_from(count).map_err(|_| {
52:             terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(
53:                 "workflow host-call count overflowed".into(),
54:             ))
55:         })?;
56:         let end = self.seq.checked_add(count).ok_or_else(|| {
57:             terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(
58:                 "workflow host-call count overflowed".into(),
59:             ))
60:         })?;
61:         if end > MAX_HOST_CALLS {
62:             return Err(terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(format!(
63:                 "workflow exceeded the maximum of {MAX_HOST_CALLS} result-bearing host calls"
64:             ))));
65:         }
66:         let start = self.seq;
67:         self.seq = end;
68:         Ok(start..end)
69:     }
70: 
71:     fn record(
72:         &mut self,
73:         seq: u64,
74:         kind: &str,
75:         hash: String,
76:         value: serde_json::Value,
77:     ) -> ScriptResult<()> {
78:         self.journal
79:             .record(seq, kind, hash, value)
80:             .map_err(journal_fatal)
81:     }
82: }
83: 
84: type ScriptResult<T> = Result<T, Box<EvalAltResult>>;
85: 
86: enum PendingAgent {
87:     Replayed(serde_json::Value),
88:     Live {
89:         seq: u64,
90:         hash: String,
91:         reply_rx: oneshot::Receiver<Result<crate::host::AgentResult, HostError>>,
92:     },
93: }
94: 
95: fn drain_parallel_replies(pending: Vec<PendingAgent>) {
96:     for entry in pending {
97:         if let PendingAgent::Live { reply_rx, .. } = entry {
98:             let _ = reply_rx.blocking_recv();
99:         }
100:     }
101: }
102: 
103: pub fn run_workflow(params: WorkflowRunParams) -> WorkflowOutcome {
104:     let WorkflowRunParams {
105:         script,
106:         args,
107:         journal,
108:         host_tx,
109:         cancel,
110:         max_ops,
111:     } = params;
112: 
113:     let ctx = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Ctx {
114:         host_tx,
115:         journal,
116:         seq: 0,
117:     }));
118: 
119:     let mut engine = rhai::Engine::new();
120:     engine.set_max_operations(max_ops);
121:     engine.set_max_call_levels(64);
122:     engine.set_max_expr_depths(128, 64);
123:     engine.set_max_string_size(16 * 1024 * 1024);
124:     engine.set_max_array_size(65_536);
125:     engine.set_max_map_size(65_536);
126:     engine.set_module_resolver(rhai::module_resolvers::DummyModuleResolver::new());
127:     engine.disable_symbol("eval");
128:     engine.register_fn("timestamp", || -> ScriptResult<()> {
129:         Err(runtime_error(
130:             "timestamp() is unavailable: workflow scripts must be deterministic (wall-clock \
131:              time breaks resume). Pass timestamps in via `args` instead.",
132:         ))
133:     });
134:     engine.register_fn("sleep", |_seconds: i64| -> ScriptResult<()> {
135:         Err(runtime_error(
136:             "sleep() is unavailable in workflow scripts — host calls already block until \
137:              their work finishes.",
138:         ))
139:     });
140:     engine.register_fn("sleep", |_seconds: f64| -> ScriptResult<()> {
141:         Err(runtime_error(
142:             "sleep() is unavailable in workflow scripts — host calls already block until \
143:              their work finishes.",
144:         ))
145:     });
146:     engine.register_fn("exit", || -> ScriptResult<()> {
147:         Err(runtime_error(
148:             "exit() is unavailable — end a workflow with complete(value) or pause(kind, msg).",
149:         ))
150:     });
151: 
152:     engine.on_progress(move |_ops| {
153:         if cancel.is_cancelled() {
154:             Some(Dynamic::from(ControlToken::Cancelled))
155:         } else {
156:             None
157:         }
158:     });
159: 
160:     register_host_fns(&mut engine, &ctx);
161: 
162:     let ast = match engine.compile(&script) {
163:         Ok(ast) => ast,
164:         Err(e) => {
165:             return WorkflowOutcome::Failed {
166:                 error: format!("script failed to compile: {e}"),
167:             };
168:         }
169:     };
170: 
171:     let mut scope = rhai::Scope::new();
172:     let args_dyn = match rhai::serde::to_dynamic(&args) {
173:         Ok(d) => d,
174:         Err(e) => {
175:             return WorkflowOutcome::Failed {
176:                 error: format!("invalid workflow args: {e}"),
177:             };
178:         }
179:     };
180:     scope.push_dynamic("args", args_dyn);
181: 
182:     match engine.eval_ast_with_scope::<Dynamic>(&mut scope, &ast) {
183:         Ok(value) => WorkflowOutcome::Completed {
184:             result: dynamic_to_value(value),
185:         },
186:         Err(err) => outcome_from_error(*err),
187:     }
188: }
189: 
190: fn outcome_from_error(err: EvalAltResult) -> WorkflowOutcome {
191:     if let Some(token) = find_control_token(&err) {
192:         return match token {
193:             ControlToken::Complete(result) => WorkflowOutcome::Completed { result },
194:             ControlToken::Pause(kind, message) => WorkflowOutcome::Paused { kind, message },
195:             ControlToken::Budget(message) => WorkflowOutcome::BudgetExceeded { message },
196:             ControlToken::Cancelled => WorkflowOutcome::Cancelled,
197:             ControlToken::Fatal(error) => WorkflowOutcome::Failed { error },
198:         };
199:     }
200:     WorkflowOutcome::Failed {
201:         error: crate::with_rhai_hint(err.to_string()),
202:     }
203: }
204: 
205: fn find_control_token(err: &EvalAltResult) -> Option<ControlToken> {
206:     match err {
207:         EvalAltResult::ErrorTerminated(token, _) => token.clone().try_cast::<ControlToken>(),
208:         EvalAltResult::ErrorInFunctionCall(_, _, inner, _) => find_control_token(inner),
209:         EvalAltResult::ErrorInModule(_, inner, _) => find_control_token(inner),
210:         _ => None,
211:     }
212: }
213: 
214: fn terminated(token: ControlToken) -> Box<EvalAltResult> {
215:     Box::new(EvalAltResult::ErrorTerminated(
216:         Dynamic::from(token),
217:         Position::NONE,
218:     ))
219: }
220: 
221: fn runtime_error(message: impl Into<String>) -> Box<EvalAltResult> {
222:     Box::new(EvalAltResult::ErrorRuntime(
223:         Dynamic::from(message.into()),
224:         Position::NONE,
225:     ))
226: }
227: 
228: fn journal_fatal(error: JournalError) -> Box<EvalAltResult> {
229:     terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(error.to_string()))
230: }
231: 
232: fn dynamic_to_value(d: Dynamic) -> serde_json::Value {
233:     rhai::serde::from_dynamic::<serde_json::Value>(&d).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null)
234: }
235: 
236: fn value_to_dynamic(v: &serde_json::Value) -> ScriptResult<Dynamic> {
237:     rhai::serde::to_dynamic(v).map_err(|e| runtime_error(format!("host result conversion: {e}")))
238: }
239: 
240: fn map_to_value(map: rhai::Map) -> ScriptResult<serde_json::Value> {
241:     rhai::serde::from_dynamic::<serde_json::Value>(&Dynamic::from_map(map))
242:         .map_err(|e| runtime_error(format!("invalid options map: {e}")))
243: }
244: 
245: fn host_call<T>(
246:     ctx: &Rc<RefCell<Ctx>>,
247:     kind: &'static str,
248:     payload: serde_json::Value,
249:     build: impl FnOnce(oneshot::Sender<Result<T, HostError>>) -> WorkflowHostRequest,
250:     to_result: impl FnOnce(T) -> serde_json::Value,
251: ) -> ScriptResult<serde_json::Value> {
252:     let hash = request_hash(kind, &payload);
253:     let seq = ctx.borrow_mut().next_seq()?;
254: 
255:     match ctx.borrow().journal.replay(seq, kind, &hash) {
256:         Ok(Some(recorded)) => {
257:             if let Some(err) = replay_host_error(&recorded) {
258:                 return Err(err);
259:             }
260:             return Ok(recorded);
261:         }
262:         Ok(None) => {}
263:         Err(error) => return Err(journal_fatal(error)),
264:     }
265: 
266:     let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = oneshot::channel();
267:     ctx.borrow()
268:         .host_tx
269:         .send(build(reply_tx))
270:         .map_err(|_| terminated(ControlToken::Fatal("workflow host channel closed".into())))?;
271: 
272:     let reply = reply_rx
273:         .blocking_recv()
274:         .map_err(|_| terminated(ControlToken::Fatal("workflow host dropped reply".into())))?;
275: 
276:     let value = match reply {
277:         Ok(v) => to_result(v),
278:         Err(HostError::AgentCallQuotaExceeded { requested, maximum }) => {
279:             return Err(runtime_error(format!(
280:                 "workflow agent-call quota exceeded: requested {requested}, maximum {maximum}"
281:             )));
282:         }
283:         Err(HostError::BudgetExceeded) => {
284:             return Err(terminated(ControlToken::Budget(
285:                 "workflow agent budget exceeded".into(),
286:             )));
287:         }
288:         Err(HostError::Cancelled) => return Err(terminated(ControlToken::Cancelled)),
289:         Err(HostError::Unsupported(msg)) => {
290:             let sentinel = host_error_sentinel(&msg);
291:             ctx.borrow_mut().record(seq, kind, hash, sentinel)?;
292:             return Err(runtime_error(msg));
293:         }
294:         Err(HostError::Failed(msg)) => {
295:             let sentinel = host_error_sentinel(&msg);
296:             ctx.borrow_mut().record(seq, kind, hash, sentinel)?;
297:             return Err(runtime_error(msg));
298:         }
299:     };
300: 
301:     ctx.borrow_mut().record(seq, kind, hash, value.clone())?;
302:     Ok(value)
303: }

305: const HOST_TERMINAL_KEY: &str = "__xai_workflow_parallel_terminal";
306: const TERMINAL_BUDGET: &str = "budget_exceeded";
307: const TERMINAL_CANCELLED: &str = "cancelled";
308: const TERMINAL_DROPPED_REPLY: &str = "dropped_reply";

310: fn host_error_sentinel(message: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
311:     serde_json::json!({ HOST_ERROR_KEY: message })
312: }

314: fn replay_host_error(recorded: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<Box<rhai::EvalAltResult>> {
315:     let message = recorded.get(HOST_ERROR_KEY)?.as_str()?;
316:     Some(runtime_error(message.to_string()))
317: }

319: fn host_terminal_sentinel(kind: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
320:     serde_json::json!({ HOST_TERMINAL_KEY: kind })
321: }

323: fn host_terminal_error(kind: &str) -> Box<rhai::EvalAltResult> {
324:     match kind {
325:         TERMINAL_BUDGET => terminated(ControlToken::Budget(
326:             "workflow agent budget exceeded".into(),
327:         )),
328:         TERMINAL_CANCELLED => terminated(ControlToken::Cancelled),
329:         TERMINAL_DROPPED_REPLY => {
330:             terminated(ControlToken::Fatal("workflow host dropped reply".into()))
331:         }
332:         _ => terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(
333:             "workflow journal contains an unknown terminal marker".into(),
334:         )),
335:     }
336: }

338: fn is_host_terminal_sentinel(recorded: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
339:     recorded.get(HOST_TERMINAL_KEY).is_some()

342: fn host_emit(ctx: &Rc<RefCell<Ctx>>, build: impl FnOnce(bool) -> WorkflowHostRequest) {
343:     let (replaying, tx) = {
344:         let ctx = ctx.borrow();
345:         (ctx.replaying(), ctx.host_tx.clone())
346:     };
347:     let _ = tx.send(build(replaying));
348: }

350: fn reserve_agent_calls(ctx: &Rc<RefCell<Ctx>>, count: usize) -> ScriptResult<()> {
351:     if count == 0 {
352:         return Ok(());
353:     }
354:     let count =
355:         u64::try_from(count).map_err(|_| runtime_error("workflow agent-call count overflowed"))?;
356:     let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = oneshot::channel();
357:     ctx.borrow()
358:         .host_tx
359:         .send(WorkflowHostRequest::ReserveAgentCalls {
360:             count,
361:             reply: reply_tx,
362:         })
363:         .map_err(|_| terminated(ControlToken::Fatal("workflow host channel closed".into())))?;
364:     match reply_rx
365:         .blocking_recv()
366:         .map_err(|_| terminated(ControlToken::Fatal("workflow host dropped reply".into())))?
367:     {
368:         Ok(()) => Ok(()),
369:         Err(HostError::AgentCallQuotaExceeded { requested, maximum }) => {
370:             Err(terminated(ControlToken::Budget(format!(
371:                 "workflow agent budget exceeded: requested {requested}, maximum {maximum}"
372:             ))))
373:         }
374:         Err(HostError::Cancelled) => Err(terminated(ControlToken::Cancelled)),
375:         Err(HostError::BudgetExceeded) => Err(terminated(ControlToken::Budget(
376:             "workflow agent budget exceeded".into(),
377:         ))),
378:         Err(HostError::Unsupported(message) | HostError::Failed(message)) => {
379:             Err(runtime_error(message))
380:         }
381:     }
382: }
383: 
384: fn release_agent_calls(ctx: &Rc<RefCell<Ctx>>, count: usize) {
385:     if count == 0 {
386:         return;
387:     }
388:     let Ok(count) = u64::try_from(count) else {
389:         return;
390:     };
391:     let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = oneshot::channel();
392:     if ctx
393:         .borrow()
394:         .host_tx
395:         .send(WorkflowHostRequest::ReleaseAgentCalls {
396:             count,
397:             reply: reply_tx,
398:         })
399:         .is_err()
400:     {
401:         return;
402:     }
403:     let _ = reply_rx.blocking_recv();
404: }

406: fn is_resumable_unjournaled_terminal(err: &EvalAltResult) -> bool {
407:     matches!(
408:         find_control_token(err),
409:         Some(ControlToken::Cancelled | ControlToken::Budget(_))
410:     )
411: }

413: fn spawn_agent_call(ctx: &Rc<RefCell<Ctx>>, opts: AgentOpts) -> ScriptResult<Dynamic> {
414:     let payload = serde_json::to_value(&opts)
415:         .map_err(|e| runtime_error(format!("invalid agent options: {e}")))?;
416:     let hash = request_hash("spawn_agent", &payload);
417:     let is_live = {
418:         let ctx = ctx.borrow();
419:         match ctx.journal.replay(ctx.seq, "spawn_agent", &hash) {
420:             Ok(Some(_)) => false,
421:             Ok(None) => true,
422:             Err(error) => return Err(journal_fatal(error)),
423:         }
424:     };
425:     if is_live {
426:         reserve_agent_calls(ctx, 1)?;
427:     }
428:     let value = match host_call(
429:         ctx,
430:         "spawn_agent",
431:         payload,
432:         |reply| WorkflowHostRequest::SpawnAgent { opts, reply },
433:         |result| serde_json::to_value(result).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null),
434:     ) {
435:         Ok(value) => value,
436:         Err(err) => {
437:             if is_live && is_resumable_unjournaled_terminal(&err) {
438:                 release_agent_calls(ctx, 1);
439:             }
440:             return Err(err);
441:         }
442:     };
443:     value_to_dynamic(&value)
444: }

446: fn agent_opts_from_map(prompt: Option<&str>, map: rhai::Map) -> ScriptResult<AgentOpts> {
447:     let value = map_to_value(map)?;
448:     let mut opts: AgentOpts = serde_json::from_value(value)
449:         .map_err(|e| runtime_error(format!("invalid agent options: {e}")))?;
450:     if let Some(prompt) = prompt {
451:         opts.prompt = prompt.to_string();
452:     }
453:     if opts.prompt.trim().is_empty() {
454:         return Err(runtime_error("agent prompt must not be empty"));
455:     }
456:     Ok(opts)
457: }

459: fn register_host_fns(engine: &mut rhai::Engine, ctx: &Rc<RefCell<Ctx>>) {
460:     let c = ctx.clone();
461:     engine.register_fn("agent", move |prompt: &str| -> ScriptResult<Dynamic> {
462:         spawn_agent_call(
463:             &c,
464:             AgentOpts {
465:                 prompt: prompt.to_string(),
466:                 ..Default::default()
467:             },
468:         )
469:     });
470:     let c = ctx.clone();
471:     engine.register_fn(
472:         "agent",
473:         move |prompt: &str, opts: rhai::Map| -> ScriptResult<Dynamic> {
474:             let opts = agent_opts_from_map(Some(prompt), opts)?;
475:             spawn_agent_call(&c, opts)
476:         },
477:     );
478: 
479:     let c = ctx.clone();
480:     engine.register_fn(
481:         "parallel",
482:         move |items: rhai::Array| -> ScriptResult<rhai::Array> {
483:             if items.len() > MAX_PARALLEL {
484:                 return Err(runtime_error(format!(
485:                     "parallel() accepts at most {MAX_PARALLEL} items per call (got {})",
486:                     items.len()
487:                 )));
488:             }
489:             let mut opts_list = Vec::with_capacity(items.len());
490:             for item in items {
491:                 let map = item
492:                     .try_cast::<rhai::Map>()
493:                     .ok_or_else(|| runtime_error("parallel() items must be option maps"))?;
494:                 opts_list.push(agent_opts_from_map(None, map)?);
495:             }
496: 
497:             let requests = opts_list
498:                 .into_iter()
499:                 .map(|opts| {
500:                     let payload = serde_json::to_value(&opts)
501:                         .map_err(|e| runtime_error(format!("invalid agent options: {e}")))?;
502:                     Ok((opts, request_hash("spawn_agent", &payload)))
503:                 })
504:                 .collect::<ScriptResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
505:             let live_count = {
506:                 let ctx = c.borrow();
507:                 let mut seq = ctx.seq;
508:                 let mut live = 0usize;
509:                 for (_, hash) in &requests {
510:                     match ctx.journal.replay(seq, "spawn_agent", hash) {
511:                         Ok(Some(_)) => {}
512:                         Ok(None) => live += 1,
513:                         Err(error) => return Err(journal_fatal(error)),
514:                     }
515:                     seq = seq.checked_add(1).ok_or_else(|| {
516:                         terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(
517:                             "workflow host-call count overflowed".into(),
518:                         ))
519:                     })?;
520:                 }
521:                 live
522:             };
523:             reserve_agent_calls(&c, live_count)?;
524:             let mut pending = Vec::with_capacity(requests.len());
525:             for (opts, hash) in requests {
526:                 let seq = c.borrow_mut().next_seq().inspect_err(|_| {
527:                     drain_parallel_replies(std::mem::take(&mut pending));
528:                 })?;
529:                 match c.borrow().journal.replay(seq, "spawn_agent", &hash) {
530:                     Ok(Some(value)) => pending.push(PendingAgent::Replayed(value)),
531:                     Ok(None) => {
532:                         let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = oneshot::channel();
533:                         if c.borrow()
534:                             .host_tx
535:                             .send(WorkflowHostRequest::SpawnAgent {
536:                                 opts,
537:                                 reply: reply_tx,
538:                             })
539:                             .is_err()
540:                         {
541:                             drain_parallel_replies(pending);
542:                             return Err(terminated(ControlToken::Fatal(
543:                                 "workflow host channel closed".into(),
544:                             )));
545:                         }
546:                         pending.push(PendingAgent::Live {
547:                             seq,
548:                             hash,
549:                             reply_rx,
550:                         });
551:                     }
552:                     Err(error) => {
553:                         drain_parallel_replies(pending);
554:                         return Err(journal_fatal(error));
555:                     }
556:                 }
557:             }
558: 
559:             let mut resolved: Vec<(Option<(u64, String)>, serde_json::Value)> =
560:                 Vec::with_capacity(pending.len());
561:             let mut terminal_kind: Option<String> = None;
562:             let mut terminal_error = None;
563:             let mut resumable_terminal = false;
564:             for entry in pending {
565:                 match entry {
566:                     PendingAgent::Replayed(value) => {
567:                         if is_host_terminal_sentinel(&value) {
568:                             let kind = value
569:                                 .get(HOST_TERMINAL_KEY)
570:                                 .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
571:                                 .unwrap_or("unknown")
572:                                 .to_string();
573:                             if kind == TERMINAL_BUDGET || kind == TERMINAL_CANCELLED {
574:                                 terminal_kind.get_or_insert(kind);
575:                                 resumable_terminal = true;
576:                             } else {
577:                                 terminal_kind.get_or_insert(kind);
578:                             }
579:                             continue;
580:                         }
581:                         if let Some(error) = replay_host_error(&value) {
582:                             terminal_error.get_or_insert(error);
583:                             continue;
584:                         }
585:                         resolved.push((None, value));
586:                     }
587:                     PendingAgent::Live {
588:                         seq,
589:                         hash,
590:                         reply_rx,
591:                     } => {
592:                         let value = match reply_rx.blocking_recv() {
593:                             Ok(Ok(result)) => {
594:                                 serde_json::to_value(result).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null)
595:                             }
596:                             Ok(Err(HostError::BudgetExceeded)) => {
597:                                 terminal_kind.get_or_insert_with(|| TERMINAL_BUDGET.to_string());
598:                                 resumable_terminal = true;
599:                                 host_terminal_sentinel(TERMINAL_BUDGET)
600:                             }
601:                             Ok(Err(HostError::Cancelled)) => {
602:                                 terminal_kind.get_or_insert_with(|| TERMINAL_CANCELLED.to_string());
603:                                 resumable_terminal = true;
604:                                 host_terminal_sentinel(TERMINAL_CANCELLED)
605:                             }
606:                             Err(_) => {
607:                                 terminal_kind
608:                                     .get_or_insert_with(|| TERMINAL_DROPPED_REPLY.to_string());
609:                                 host_terminal_sentinel(TERMINAL_DROPPED_REPLY)
610:                             }
611:                             Ok(Err(
612:                                 HostError::AgentCallQuotaExceeded { .. }
613:                                 | HostError::Unsupported(_)
614:                                 | HostError::Failed(_),
615:                             )) => serde_json::Value::Null,
616:                         };
617:                         resolved.push((Some((seq, hash)), value));
618:                     }
619:                 }
620:             }
621: 
622:             if resumable_terminal {
623:                 release_agent_calls(&c, live_count);
624:             } else {
625:                 for (live, value) in &resolved {
626:                     let Some((seq, hash)) = live else {
627:                         continue;
628:                     };
629:                     if let Err(error) =
630:                         c.borrow_mut()
631:                             .record(*seq, "spawn_agent", hash.clone(), value.clone())
632:                     {
633:                         terminal_error.get_or_insert(error);
634:                         break;
635:                     }
636:                 }
637:             }
638: 
639:             if let Some(kind) = terminal_kind {
640:                 return Err(host_terminal_error(&kind));
641:             }
642:             if let Some(error) = terminal_error {
643:                 return Err(error);
644:             }
645: 
646:             let mut results = rhai::Array::with_capacity(resolved.len());
647:             for (_, value) in resolved {
648:                 match value_to_dynamic(&value) {
649:                     Ok(value) => results.push(value),
650:                     Err(error) => return Err(error),
651:                 }
652:             }
653:             Ok(results)
654:         },
655:     );

48: /// Bridges the `ToolRegistry` into a session layer.
49: ///
50: /// Owns the registry and dispatches tool calls via `call_new_tool()`.
51: /// All state lives in `Resources` on the registry — no separate `ToolState`.
52: ///
53: /// # Cancellation Safety
54: ///
55: /// The `terminal` field is stored separately from the registry lock to enable
56: /// cancellation during tool execution. When a bash command is running, the
57: /// registry lock is held by `call()`. If the user cancels, `kill_foreground_commands()`
58: /// needs to access the terminal without blocking on the lock.
59: #[derive(Clone)]
60: pub struct ToolBridge {
61:     registry: Arc<FinalizedToolset>,
62:     terminal: Option<Arc<dyn TerminalBackend>>,
63: }
64: 
65: impl ToolBridge {
66:     pub fn get_builder() -> ToolRegistryBuilder {
67:         ToolRegistryBuilder::new()
68:     }

70:     pub async fn finalize_builder(
71:         builder: ToolRegistryBuilder,
72:         config: ToolServerConfig,
73:         ctx: SessionContext,
74:     ) -> Result<Self, xai_tool_runtime::ToolError> {
75:         let finalized_toolset = builder.finalize(config, ctx).map_err(|errs| {
76:             xai_tool_runtime::ToolError::invalid_arguments(format!(
77:                 "Requirements unsatisfied: {errs:?}"
78:             ))
79:         })?;
80: 
81:         let terminal;
82:         {
83:             terminal = finalized_toolset
84:                 .resources
85:                 .lock()
86:                 .await
87:                 .get::<Terminal>()
88:                 .map(|t| t.0.clone());
89:         }
90: 
91:         Ok(Self {
92:             registry: Arc::new(finalized_toolset),
93:             terminal,
94:         })
95:     }

272:     /// Seed the SkillDiscoveryTracker with session context and startup skills.
273:     ///
274:     /// Must be called at session start so the `SkillDiscoveryReminder` can
275:     /// discover skills in subdirectories.
276:     /// `display_cwd`: If set (forked sessions), skill paths in
277:     /// model-visible announcements are rewritten from real cwd to this
278:     /// value. Runtime invocation uses the real path.
279:     pub async fn seed_skill_discovery(
280:         &self,
281:         cwd: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
282:         git_root: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
283:         startup_skills: Vec<crate::implementations::skills::types::SkillInfo>,
284:         display_cwd: Option<String>,
285:         context_window_tokens: Option<u64>,
286:         skill_budget_percent: Option<f64>,
287:         compat: crate::types::compat::CompatConfig,
288:     ) {
289:         let registry = &*self.registry;
290:         let mut res = registry.resources.lock().await;
291:         // Resolve client-facing tool names from the template renderer
292:         // so listing headers and descriptions use the correct (possibly randomized) names.
293:         let renderer = res.get::<TemplateRenderer>();
294:         let skill_tool_name = renderer.and_then(|r| r.render("${{ tools.by_kind.skill }}").ok());
295:         let read_tool_name = renderer.and_then(|r| r.render("${{ tools.by_kind.read }}").ok());
296:         let tracker = res.get_or_default::<crate::types::skill_discovery_tracker::SkillManager>();
297:         if let Some(name) = skill_tool_name {
298:             tracker.set_skill_tool_name(name);
299:         }
300:         if let Some(name) = read_tool_name {
301:             tracker.set_read_tool_name(name);
302:         }
303:         tracker.set_compat(compat);
304:         tracker.seed(
305:             cwd,
306:             git_root,
307:             startup_skills,
308:             display_cwd,
309:             context_window_tokens,
310:             skill_budget_percent,
311:         );
312:     }

551:     /// Snapshot the session's scheduled tasks; empty when no scheduler is
552:     /// registered or the actor has stopped.
553:     pub async fn list_scheduled_tasks(
554:         &self,
555:     ) -> Vec<crate::implementations::grok_build::scheduler::types::ScheduledTask> {
556:         use crate::implementations::grok_build::scheduler::types::{
557:             SchedulerCommand, SchedulerHandle,
558:         };
559:         let sender = {
560:             let res = self.registry.resources.lock().await;
561:             match res.get::<SchedulerHandle>() {
562:                 Some(handle) => handle.0.clone(),
563:                 None => return Vec::new(),
564:             }
565:         };
566:         let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
567:         if sender
568:             .send(SchedulerCommand::List { reply: reply_tx })
569:             .is_err()
570:         {
571:             return Vec::new();
572:         }
573:         reply_rx
574:             .await
575:             .map(|snapshot| snapshot.tasks)
576:             .unwrap_or_default()
577:     }

579:     pub async fn delete_scheduled_task(
580:         &self,
581:         task_id: &str,
582:     ) -> Result<bool, xai_tool_runtime::ToolError> {
583:         use crate::implementations::grok_build::scheduler::types::{
584:             SchedulerCommand, SchedulerHandle,
585:         };
586:         let sender = {
587:             let res = self.registry.resources.lock().await;
588:             res.get::<SchedulerHandle>()
589:                 .ok_or_else(|| {
590:                     xai_tool_runtime::ToolError::custom("missing_resource", "SchedulerHandle")
591:                 })?
592:                 .0
593:                 .clone()
594:         };
595:         let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
596:         sender
597:             .send(SchedulerCommand::Delete {
598:                 id: task_id.to_owned(),
599:                 reply: reply_tx,
600:             })
601:             .map_err(|_| {
602:                 xai_tool_runtime::ToolError::custom("process_manager", "Scheduler actor stopped")
603:             })?;
604:         reply_rx
605:             .await
606:             .map_err(|_| {
607:                 xai_tool_runtime::ToolError::custom(
608:                     "process_manager",
609:                     "Scheduler actor dropped reply",

634:     /// Drain newly-completed bash background tasks not yet reported.
635:     /// Marks returned tasks in [`ReportedTaskCompletions`] to prevent
636:     /// duplicate reminders from [`TaskCompletionReminder`]. Reserved IDs stay
637:     /// unreported for a later genuine user turn.
638:     pub async fn drain_between_turn_bash_completions(
639:         &self,
640:         reserved_ids: &[String],
641:     ) -> Vec<TaskSnapshot> {
642:         let tasks = match self.list_tasks().await {
643:             Some(t) => t,
644:             None => return Vec::new(),
645:         };
646:         let completed: Vec<TaskSnapshot> = tasks
647:             .into_iter()
648:             .filter(|t| t.completed && t.kind != TaskKind::Monitor)
649:             .collect();
650:         if completed.is_empty() {
651:             return Vec::new();
652:         }
653: 
654:         use crate::reminders::task_completion::{ReportedTaskCompletions, task_owned_by_session};
655: 
656:         let mut res = self.registry.resources.lock().await;
657:         // Subagents share the parent's terminal backend, so `list_tasks()`
658:         // returns tasks owned by other sessions. Scope the between-turn
659:         // "While you were idle, … background task completed" drain to tasks
660:         // this session owns, mirroring the per-tool-call
661:         // `TaskCompletionReminder` filter — otherwise a parent (or sibling)
662:         // bash task that finished mid-subagent-turn leaks its completion
663:         // `<system-reminder>` into the subagent's conversation. The owner
664:         // filter runs before `mark_reported` so the owning session still
665:         // reports the task on its own next turn.
666:         let my_owner = res.get::<OwnerSessionId>().map(|o| o.0.clone());
667:         let state = res.get_or_default::<State<ReportedTaskCompletions>>();
668:         completed
669:             .into_iter()
670:             .filter(|t| task_owned_by_session(t, my_owner.as_deref()))
671:             .filter(|t| !reserved_ids.contains(&t.task_id))
672:             .filter(|t| state.mark_reported(&t.task_id))
673:             .collect()
674:     }

44: /// Dispatch a `pre_tool_use` event against all matching hooks.
45: ///
46: /// Runs hooks sequentially in config order. Only an explicit `deny`
47: /// decision from a hook stops the chain and blocks the tool call.
48: ///
49: /// Hook failures (timeouts, crashes, command-not-found, env-var
50: /// pre-spawn refusals, malformed output) are **fail-open**: the failure
51: /// is logged and surfaced in the per-hook results for the UI scrollback,
52: /// but the tool call continues as if the hook had allowed it. Grok
53: /// runs in protected environments where induced-failure bypass of
54: /// security hooks is not part of the threat model; the previous
55: /// fail-closed posture over-blocked innocent tool calls when
56: /// hooks timed out or had unrelated configuration errors.
57: ///
58: /// Returns `Allow` if no hooks match, all hooks allow, or all failing
59: /// hooks are non-blocking by virtue of this fail-open policy.
60: pub async fn dispatch_pre_tool_use(
61:     registry: &HookRegistry,
62:     envelope: &HookEventEnvelope,
63:     ctx: &RunContext<'_>,
64: ) -> PreToolUseResult {
65:     let hooks = registry.hooks_for(HookEventName::PreToolUse);
66:     if hooks.is_empty() {
67:         return PreToolUseResult {
68:             decision: HookDecision::Allow,
69:             results: Vec::new(),
70:         };
71:     }
72: 
73:     let span = dispatch_span(HookEventName::PreToolUse, hooks.len());
74:     let _enter = span.enter();
75: 
76:     let match_value = envelope.payload.match_value().map(str::to_string);
77:     let mut run_results = Vec::new();
78: 
79:     for spec in hooks {
80:         if !eligible_or_record_skip(spec, match_value.as_deref(), &mut run_results) {
81:             continue;
82:         }
83: 
84:         let _hook_span = tracing::info_span!(
85:             "hook.run",
86:             hook_name = %spec.name,
87:             hook_event = %HookEventName::PreToolUse,
88:         )
89:         .entered();
90: 
91:         let (result, elapsed, http_info) =
92:             runner::run_hook(spec, envelope, ctx, GateKind::Tool).await;
93: 
94:         match result {
95:             HookRunnerResult::Decision(HookDecision::Deny { reason, .. }) => {
96:                 tracing::info!(
97:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
98:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
99:                     reason = %reason,
100:                     "hook denied"
101:                 );
102:                 run_results.push(HookRunResult::Blocked {
103:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
104:                     detail: format!("denied: {reason}"),
105:                     elapsed,
106:                     http_info,
107:                 });
108:                 record_dispatch_counts(&span, &run_results);
109:                 return PreToolUseResult {
110:                     decision: HookDecision::Deny {
111:                         reason,
112:                         hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
113:                     },
114:                     results: run_results,
115:                 };
116:             }
117:             HookRunnerResult::Decision(HookDecision::Allow) => {
118:                 tracing::info!(
119:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
120:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
121:                     "hook allowed"
122:                 );
123:                 run_results.push(HookRunResult::Success {
124:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
125:                     elapsed,
126:                     http_info,
127:                 });
128:             }
129:             HookRunnerResult::Failed(err) => {
130:                 tracing::warn!(
131:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
132:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
133:                     error = %err,
134:                     "hook failed; ignoring (fail-open)"
135:                 );
136:                 run_results.push(HookRunResult::Failed {
137:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
138:                     error: err.clone(),
139:                     elapsed,
140:                     http_info,
141:                 });
142:             }
143:             HookRunnerResult::Success | HookRunnerResult::Stop(_) => {

145:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
146:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
147:                     "hook completed"

149:                 run_results.push(HookRunResult::Success {
150:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
151:                     elapsed,
152:                     http_info,
153:                 });
154:             }

322:                                 .unwrap_or_else(|| "stopped by hook".to_string())
323:                         }),
324:                         additional_context: outcome.additional_context,
325:                     },
326:                 );
327:             }
328:             HookRunnerResult::Failed(err) => {
329:                 tracing::warn!(
330:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
331:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
332:                     error = %err,
333:                     "stop hook failed; ignoring (fail-open)"
334:                 );
335:                 out.results.push(HookRunResult::Failed {
336:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
337:                     error: err,
338:                     elapsed,
339:                     http_info,
340:                 });
341:             }
342:             HookRunnerResult::Success | HookRunnerResult::Decision(_) => {
343:                 out.results.push(HookRunResult::Success {
344:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
345:                     elapsed,
346:                     http_info,
347:                 });
348:             }
349:         }
350:     }
351: 
352:     record_dispatch_counts(&span, &out.results);
353:     out
354: }

356: /// Dispatch an observe-only event against all matching hooks; never denies.
357: pub async fn dispatch_non_blocking(
358:     registry: &HookRegistry,
359:     event: HookEventName,
360:     envelope: &HookEventEnvelope,
361:     ctx: &RunContext<'_>,
362: ) -> Vec<HookRunResult> {
363:     debug_assert!(
364:         event.traits().gate == GateKind::Observe,
365:         "dispatch_non_blocking called with gate event {event:?}"
366:     );
367:     let hooks = registry.hooks_for_canonical(event);
368:     if hooks.is_empty() {
369:         return Vec::new();
370:     }
371: 
372:     let span = dispatch_span(event, hooks.len());
373:     let _enter = span.enter();
374: 
375:     let match_value = envelope.payload.match_value().map(str::to_string);
376:     let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(hooks.len());
377: 
378:     for spec in hooks {
379:         if !eligible_or_record_skip(spec, match_value.as_deref(), &mut results) {
380:             continue;
381:         }
382: 
383:         let _hook_span = tracing::info_span!(
384:             "hook.run",
385:             hook_name = %spec.name,
386:             hook_event = %event,
387:         )
388:         .entered();
389: 
390:         let (result, elapsed, http_info) =
391:             runner::run_hook(spec, envelope, ctx, GateKind::Observe).await;
392: 
393:         match result {
394:             HookRunnerResult::Success => {
395:                 tracing::info!(
396:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
397:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
398:                     "hook completed"
399:                 );
400:                 results.push(HookRunResult::Success {
401:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
402:                     elapsed,
403:                     http_info,
404:                 });
405:             }
406:             HookRunnerResult::Failed(err) => {
407:                 tracing::warn!(
408:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
409:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
410:                     error = %err,
411:                     "hook failed"
412:                 );
413:                 results.push(HookRunResult::Failed {
414:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
415:                     error: err,
416:                     elapsed,
417:                     http_info,
418:                 });
419:             }
420:             HookRunnerResult::Decision(_) | HookRunnerResult::Stop(_) => {
421:                 tracing::info!(
422:                     hook_name = %spec.name,
423:                     elapsed_ms = elapsed.as_millis() as u64,
424:                     "hook completed"
425:                 );
426:                 results.push(HookRunResult::Success {
427:                     hook_name: spec.name.clone(),
428:                     elapsed,
429:                     http_info,
430:                 });
431:             }
432:         }
433:     }
434: 
435:     record_dispatch_counts(&span, &results);
436: 
437:     results
438: }
439: 
440: fn record_dispatch_counts(span: &tracing::Span, results: &[HookRunResult]) {
441:     let mut num_success = 0i64;
442:     let mut num_failed = 0i64;
443:     let mut num_skipped = 0i64;
444:     let mut total_duration_ms = 0i64;
445:     let mut num_blocked = 0i64;
446:     for r in results {
447:         match r {
448:             HookRunResult::Success { elapsed, .. } => {
449:                 num_success += 1;
450:                 total_duration_ms += elapsed.as_millis() as i64;
451:             }
452:             HookRunResult::Blocked { elapsed, .. } => {
453:                 num_blocked += 1;
454:                 total_duration_ms += elapsed.as_millis() as i64;
455:             }
456:             HookRunResult::Failed { elapsed, .. } => {
457:                 num_failed += 1;
458:                 total_duration_ms += elapsed.as_millis() as i64;
459:             }
460:             HookRunResult::Skipped { .. } => num_skipped += 1,
461:         }
462:     }
463:     span.record("num_success", num_success);
464:     span.record("num_failed", num_failed);
465:     span.record("num_blocking", num_blocked);
466:     span.record("num_skipped", num_skipped);
467:     span.record("total_duration_ms", total_duration_ms);
468: }

285:                 | "--sort"

287:                 | "-q"

289:                 | "-u"
290:                 | "-U"
291:                 | "-g"

293:                 | "-C"
294:                 | "-s"

297:                 | "--sid"

328:         // Short cluster ending in arg-taking `o`/`O` (`-eo etime`, `-axo cmd`):
329:         // next word is the format list, not an option cluster.
330:         if s.starts_with('-') && !s.starts_with("--") && s.ends_with(['o', 'O']) {
331:             skip_next = true;
332:             continue;
333:         }
334:     }
335:     false
336: }

338: /// Check whether the command words (already parsed by tree-sitter) match one of
339: /// the known safe command prefixes.
340: fn is_safe_command_words(words: &[String]) -> bool {
341:     if words.is_empty() {
342:         return false;
343:     }
344:     if rg_has_pre_flag(words) {
345:         return false;
346:     }
347:     if kubectl_has_unsafe_flag(words) {
348:         return false;
349:     }
350:     if ps_dumps_environment(words) {
351:         return false;
352:     }
353:     let joined = words.join(" ");
354:     is_safe_command_words_str(&joined)
355: }
356: 
357: fn matches_command_prefix(cmd: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
358:     cmd == pattern || (cmd.starts_with(pattern) && cmd.as_bytes().get(pattern.len()) == Some(&b' '))
359: }
360: 
361: /// Shared prefix check used by both the tree-sitter path and the fallback path.
362: fn is_safe_command_words_str(cmd: &str) -> bool {
363:     matches_command_prefix(cmd, "ls")
364:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "cat")
365:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "pwd")
366:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "date")
367:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git status")
368:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git branch")
369:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git log")
370:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git diff")
371:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git ls-files")
372:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git show")
373:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "git rev-parse")
374:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "whoami")
375:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "hostname")
376:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "uptime")
377:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "grep")
378:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "rg")
379:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "kubectl get")
380:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "kubectl logs")
381:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "kubectl describe")
382:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "ps")
383:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "bin/explorer ls")
384:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "head")
385:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "tail")
386:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "wc")
387:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "sort")
388:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "uniq")
389:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "tr")
390:         || matches_command_prefix(cmd, "cut")
391:     // CWE-863: `tee` removed from safe-command list — it writes stdin
392:     // to arbitrary files, enabling pipelines like `cat data | tee /target` to
393:     // bypass edit permissions.
394:     //
395:     // `rg --pre` is excluded at the words level via [`rg_has_pre_flag`] — the
396:     // string form here cannot see flag structure reliably after join.
397: }

399: /// Commands which are always safe to execute and should never prompt the user.
400: /// This list is checked against the primary command after bash command splitting/parsing.
401: const ALWAYS_SAFE_COMMANDS: &[&str] = &[
402:     // Read-only filesystem commands
403:     "ls",
404:     "cat",
405:     "pwd",
406:     "date",
407:     "whoami",
408:     "hostname",
409:     "uptime",
410:     "ps",
411:     // Git read-only commands
412:     "git status",
413:     "git branch",
414:     "git log",
415:     "git diff",
416:     "git ls-files",
417:     "git show",
418:     "git rev-parse",
419:     // Search commands
420:     "grep",
421:     "rg",
422:     // Kubernetes read-only commands
423:     "kubectl get",
424:     "kubectl logs",
425:     "kubectl describe",
426:     // Internal tooling
427:     "bin/explorer ls",
428: ];
429: 
430: /// Check whether parsed command words match the always-safe list.
431: ///
432: /// Applied per chained segment so that scripts like `ls && rm -rf /` cannot
433: /// auto-approve via the always-safe primary alone — every non-setup segment
434: /// must independently pass this (or the broader `is_safe_command_words`,
435: /// or a user whitelist) check.
436: fn is_always_safe_command_words(words: &[String]) -> bool {
437:     if words.is_empty() {
438:         return false;
439:     }
440:     if rg_has_pre_flag(words) {
441:         return false;
442:     }
443:     if kubectl_has_unsafe_flag(words) {
444:         return false;
445:     }
446:     if ps_dumps_environment(words) {
447:         return false;
448:     }
449: 
450:     let joined = words.join(" ");
451: 
452:     // CWE-183: use matches_command_prefix to require a word boundary after
453:     // the safe prefix, preventing e.g. "tr" from matching "truncate".
454:     for safe_pattern in ALWAYS_SAFE_COMMANDS {
455:         if matches_command_prefix(&joined, safe_pattern) {
456:             return true;
457:         }
458:     }
459: 
460:     false
461: }
462: 
463: /// Default always-allow whitelist scope (word count) for a parsed command.
464: ///
465: /// Safe-listed prefixes (`ls`, `grep`, `git status`, `kubectl get`, …) scope
466: /// to exactly the safe prefix: persisting it grants nothing beyond the
467: /// built-in safe-command auto-allow, while baking the first path or pattern
468: /// into the prefix made every different-arg invocation re-prompt.
469: /// Everything else keeps the first-two-words-plus-flags default, so e.g.
470: /// `sudo git status` still scopes to `sudo git`, not bare `sudo`.
471: ///
472: /// Scope narrowing applies only when the **full** invocation is safe-listed.
473: /// Otherwise a non-auto-allowed form like `rg --pre …` would still scope to
474: /// bare `rg`, and "Always allow" would re-open the preprocessor exec hole.
475: pub fn default_always_allow_scope(words: &[String]) -> usize {
476:     if words.is_empty() {
477:         return 0;
478:     }
479:     if is_safe_command_words(words) {
480:         if is_safe_command_words_str(&words[0]) {
481:             return 1;
482:         }
483:         if words.len() >= 2 && is_safe_command_words_str(&words[..2].join(" ")) {
484:             return 2;
485:         }
486:     }
487:     let mut n = words.len().min(2);
488:     while n < words.len() && words[n].starts_with('-') {
489:         n += 1;
490:     }
491:     n
492: }
493: 
494: /// Check whether parsed command words begin with a known dangerous command.
495: ///
496: /// Applied per chained segment. Critically, a segment matching this check
497: /// is NEVER auto-approved via a user whitelist — the user must always be
498: /// prompted for it. This preserves the invariant from the previous
499: /// `is_dangerous_command` script-level check, but applied to every
500: /// segment in a chain instead of only the start of the script.
501: fn is_dangerous_command_words(words: &[String]) -> bool {
502:     if words.is_empty() {
503:         return false;
504:     }
505:     let joined = words.join(" ");
506:     matches_command_prefix(&joined, "rm")
507:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "chmod")
508:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "chown")
509:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "chgrp")
510:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "chattr")
511:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "pkill")
512:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "kill")
513:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "killall")
514:         || matches_command_prefix(&joined, "git push")
515: }
516: 
517: /// Whitelist matching helper. Uses `matches_command_prefix` so that user
518: /// allow/deny entries enforce a word boundary after the prefix — preventing
519: /// the "git" entry from matching "gitleaks" (CWE-183).
520: fn matches_whitelist_prefix(segment_str: &str, allowed_prefix: &str) -> bool {
521:     matches_command_prefix(segment_str, allowed_prefix)
522: }

524: /// Ordinary command-segment outcome, before script-level effect floors.
525: #[derive(Debug)]
526: pub(crate) enum SegmentEvaluation {
527:     /// All non-setup segments safe/always-safe or on an allow-prefix.
528:     /// `via_session_grant`: at least one segment hit `allowed_bash_commands`.
529:     AutoAllow { via_session_grant: bool },
530:     /// Disallow-prefix matched; reject without prompting.
531:     Reject(String),
532:     /// One or more segments need a user decision.
533:     NeedsPrompts {
534:         #[allow(dead_code)]
535:         segments: Vec<String>,
536:         any_dangerous: bool,
537:     },
538:     /// Tree-sitter could not decompose the script (heredoc, `$(…)`,
539:     /// backtick, single `&` background, …). Caller should fall back to a
540:     /// single conservative prompt with the full script.
541:     Unparseable,
542: }

544: /// One request's parsed Bash authorization facts.
545: #[derive(Debug)]
546: struct BashEvaluation {
547:     segments: SegmentEvaluation,
548:     writes_real_file: bool,
549:     env_risk: EnvRisk,
550:     exact_grant: bool,
551:     all_segments_granted: bool,
552:     has_opaque_shell: bool,
553:     exec_risk: bool,
554:     /// Raw segment word lists for ambient cwd tracking (git present, flags clean).
555:     ambient_segments: Option<Vec<Vec<String>>>,
556: }
557: 
558: fn unparseable_exec_risk(cmd: &str) -> bool {
559:     // WHY: word-only decomposition failed; ambient git never ran. Fail closed
560:     // when the script may still invoke git so sandbox/Auto cannot auto-allow.
561:     script_may_invoke_git(cmd)
562: }
